newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Argentine oilseed crop prospects improve - Oil World.
newsitem.headline: Argentine oilseed crop prospects improve - Oil World.

text.p: Argentine oilseed production in 1996/97 is forecast at 19.3 million tonnes, slightly below this season's level but prospects are improving, the independent Hamburg-based newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.
This latest forecast is one million tonnes above the last prediction on August 9. Oil World said it also revised downward its forecast of this season's crop to 19.67 million tonnes.

It said that since then higher world prices for oilseeds had increased profit margins for Argentine farmers and this, when set against a background of falling wheat prices and steady corn, would lead to more second-crop soybeans being planted.
Also, dry weather in the region was delaying summer grain plantings, particularly of corn and sorghum.

"There are already reports that farmers are switching from summer grains to oilseeds, especially sunflowers. If sufficient rainfall is not received in the next few weeks more switching will take place," Oil World said.

It predicted the total oilseed area harvested in 1996/97 at 10.1 million hectares, down from 10.63 million this season. But soybeans will take up to 6.1 million hectares, up from 5.99 million, and sunflowers 2.86 million, down from 3.23 million. --Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
